title: Mariner Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments meet Mariner Bank's EU data residency, GDPR, GLBA/PCI controls, and log retention/redaction requirements. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated or Private for regulatory reasons. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, BAA discussion, schedule technical deep dive for network/VPC and logging configs, run pilot in EU Dedicated cluster.
topics: GDPR data subject rights and deletion
HIPAA/BAA note (customer asked for BAA reference though primary is financial)
Logging restrictions: PII redaction, retention limits, forwarding to SIEM
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
KMS/HSM key management and encryption at rest/in transit
action_items: Daniel Kim (Redwood AE): Send SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 summary, and security whitepaper - due 2025-02-14
Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Prepare ER diagram for Dedicated and Private network topology, include VPC endpoints and private link options - due 2025-02-18
Tom Reynolds (Mariner): Share existing SIEM schema and log ingestion method (Splunk) so Redwood can propose log-forwarding configuration - due 2025-02-17
Laura Chen (Mariner): Provide list of regulatory requirements (GLBA controls + PCI scoping) and whether PCI applies to LLM outputs - due 2025-02-16
next_steps: Redwood to share security artifacts (SOC2/ISO/pen test summary)
Schedule technical deep dive for Dedicated EU deployment and logging with Mariner infra team (2 weeks)
Draft pilot statement of work for a Dedicated EU cluster with log forwarding and retention policy
Confirm whether Mariner legal needs a BAA or contract language for data processing (they will confirm)
Run benchmark/ping tests from Mariner EU infra to Redwood EU region as part of pilot
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Laura Chen (Head of Security, Mariner); Michael Ortiz (CTO, Mariner); Sara Patel (Head of Data); Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated may be imperfect): Discussed data residency and compliance for deploying Redwood inference. Customer wants EU-only data residency, strict logging controls, redaction and short retention windows. Explored Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreed to share security docs and schedule tech deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Daniel Kim: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Daniel, AE for Redwood Inference, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya Nair: hi all, happy to be here. we'll focus on the compliance and networking side today.
[00:13] Laura Chen: thanks, um so high level we need to understand if data can be kept in the EU, and how logs are handled. we have pretty strict internal controls because of GLBA and some PCI scoping.
[00:24] Michael Ortiz: yeah, timeline is rapid — pilot in Q2, production by Q4 if everything looks good. but residency is a hard stop for certain workflows.
[00:33] Daniel Kim: totally understood. quick question on scope — are you considering Redwood hosted (our multi-tenant API), dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud), or private (VPC/air-gapped on-prem)? or all three?
[00:44] Sara Patel: we want options. for low-sensitivity workloads maybe hosted is ok, but anything tied to customer PII or transaction data needs to be EU-only and ideally dedicated or private.
[00:57] Laura Chen: also need to know about logs. we can't have request/response logs retained beyond 30 days for certain data classes, and we need the ability to redact PII before logs leave our environment.
[01:10] Priya Nair: right — technical note: our hosted product defaults to logging for observability, but for Dedicated we can change retention and disable request/response logging, and for Private (VPC/on-prem) logs can stay inside your network and forward to your SIEM.
[01:23] Tom Reynolds: when you say "disable request/response logging", does that also remove KV cache traces? what about embeddings and vector stores?
[01:33] Priya Nair: good question. we call out that the runtime uses KV caching for latency; cache metadata doesn't contain raw PII by default, but we do give options to toggle KV persistence and to scrub prompts before they get cached. embeddings generation can be considered sensitive; many customers run embeddings on Dedicated/Private and treat vectors as regulated — we can disable logging of embeddings and purge caches on commit.
[01:54] Michael Ortiz: and what about key management — do we manage keys, or can we integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[01:59] Daniel Kim: we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, but there is a customer-managed option for enterprise contracts.
[02:11] Laura Chen: are you SOC2 and ISO certified? we need the reports and pen test summaries.
[02:16] Daniel Kim: yes — SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we'll share redacted reports. note that we also do periodic pentests; we can share summaries.
[02:25] Sara Patel: on GDPR — how do you handle data subject requests and deletion? if a user asks for erasure, what's the flow?
[02:34] Priya Nair: for Dedicated and Private, customers control data retention and can request deletion via API. For Hosted we have processes to support data deletion requests, but customers often prefer Dedicated/Private for full control. We also provide tooling to run targeted deletion of prompts and model traces, and we can provide attestations when requests are executed.
[02:56] Laura Chen: what about cross-border fallback? if Dedicated region is saturated, do you failover to another region potentially outside EU? we cannot allow that for some datasets.
[03:07] Daniel Kim: smart routing and fallbacks are policy-driven; we can configure strict routing so workloads pinned to EU don't overflow elsewhere. we can also ensure no automatic cross-region fallback for pinned workloads — that's standard for Dedicated/Private enterprise configs.
[03:22] Tom Reynolds: are there gov/country-specific entitlements for audit logs? we need immutable audit trails for model admin actions for compliance.
[03:30] Priya Nair: yes, audit logs for console and API actions are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, Datadog). retention is configurable and we support append-only write streams to meet immutability requirements.
[03:46] Michael Ortiz: curious about PCI — if LLM outputs contain cardholder data by mistake, does Redwood have DLP or redaction before persistence?
[03:56] Priya Nair: we offer pre-ingest redaction hooks and pattern-based detectors that can mask or block PII from being stored. for strict PCI scope customers, the recommendation is Dedicated/Private plus in-line redaction/filters and no persistent logging of raw responses.
[04:13] Laura Chen: can you run inside our VPC so logs never touch your control plane?
[04:19] Daniel Kim: with Private deployment we can run the control plane in your network or offer a customer-managed control plane; for Dedicated we provide a private link so traffic doesn't traverse the public internet, and logs can be forwarded only to your endpoints.
[04:32] Sara Patel: what's the timeline and cost delta between Dedicated and Private? rough ballpark is fine.
[04:38] Daniel Kim: Dedicated is typically faster to provision (weeks) and is hosted in our managed clusters; Private/on-prem takes longer (months) due to packaging and onsite validation. cost-wise Private has higher initial install and ongoing support fees, Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity with lower ops overhead. we can share a pricing matrix.
[04:58] Tom Reynolds: network question — do you support private endpoints, peering, or transit gateway style? we prefer AWS VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink.
[05:06] Priya Nair: yes we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and transit gateway patterns depending on region and deployment. we'll diagram it in the follow-up.
[05:16] Michael Ortiz: any limitations on model variants for Private? some of our legal teams want to limit which model weights are used.
[05:23] Priya Nair: you can pin model versions and we support curated model catalogs on Dedicated/Private. model uploads and custom weights are also supported in Private deployments.
[05:33] Laura Chen: about logging retention — we require some logs to be purged within 30 days, others kept for 7 years. can Redwood support differential retention per log type?
[05:45] Daniel Kim: yes, retention policies can be configured per stream/event type — e.g., request traces 30 days, admin audit logs 7+ years. for Hosted customers some policies are managed, but enterprise Dedicated/Private offers full config.
[05:58] Sara Patel: do you do redaction at ingest or redact at rest? we need assurance logs never contain raw identifiers after retention window.
[06:06] Priya Nair: both: we can apply in-line redaction before logs are persisted and we run scheduled scrubbing jobs to ensure retention rules are enforced. we also support hashed pseudonymization and tokenization if needed.
[06:19] Michael Ortiz: legal will want contractual language around data processing agreements — is that standard?
[06:25] Daniel Kim: yes, we have DPAs, can include data residency clauses, and for health/PHI we offer BAAs when applicable. for finance we can include GLBA-specific language on request.
[06:37] Laura Chen: do you do background checks on operator access and do you expose operator access logs?
[06:43] Priya Nair: yes, operator/admin access is logged and we maintain role separation. we can provide a list of control processes in the security pack.
[06:52] Tom Reynolds: can we run a short pilot with a subset of traffic to validate latency and make sure no logs leave the EU?
[06:58] Daniel Kim: absolutely, pilot is the right approach. we usually provision a dedicated EU cluster, configure log forwarding to your Splunk instance, and run a 2–4 week pilot with realistic traffic.
[07:09] Sara Patel: how do you handle external embeddings services or third-party integrations which might send data outside?
[07:15] Priya Nair: integrations are opt-in; we can block external connectors in Dedicated/Private. if you use third-party vector DBs, we'd recommend they live in your account or VPC.
[07:24] Michael Ortiz: anything else we should flag from a compliance perspective?
[07:28] Laura Chen: vendor risk team will want to see change management, incident response, and penetration test timelines.
[07:35] Daniel Kim: we'll include those in the security pack, plus contact for incident response and SLAs for incident notification windows.
[07:42] Priya Nair: quick tech note — depending on model size and seq len we may recommend quantized variants for Dedicated to save cost; these don't change residency but we should flag for performance benchmarking.
[07:55] Tom Reynolds: ok. on the pilot scope, can we include a test for data subject erasure? we will send a sample request and expect an attestation.
[08:02] Priya Nair: yes, we'll plan a DSAR run as part of pilot acceptance criteria.
[08:09] Daniel Kim: to recap next steps: we'll send security artifacts, Priya will draw the network diagram, Tom will send SIEM ingestion schema, and we'll schedule the deep technical session.
[08:19] Laura Chen: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:22] Daniel Kim: thanks, we'll follow up with links and timeline.

(End of recording)
